question.text: Calgon is used for water treatment. Which of the following statement is NOT true about Calgon?

options.text: It is polymeric compound and is water soluble.
Calgon contains the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>nd</mi></msup></math> most abundant element by weight in the Earth's crust.
It is also known as Graham's salt.
It doesnot remove <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Ca</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ion by precipitation.

solution.text:
→2nd most abundant element is Si and it is not present in calgon Na6P6O18= (Graham's salt)(Sodium hexametaphosphate)

→ It exist in polymeric form as NaPO36 and water soluble compound

→ It removes Ca2+ in soluble ion but not by precipitation
